To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The use of multiple streams of features is beneficial for the recognition of on-line handwriting.
1) The separation of the features into statistically independent streams influences the system performance.
“The use of discrete multiple stream HMM systems is not only possible, but can also outperform the state-of-the-art for on-line handwritten word recognition.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the influence of quantized features on the recognition accuracy.
the question whether the discrete single or multiple stream HMM is more suited for on-line handwriting recognition.
the influence of the feature quantization on the performance of discrete HMMs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of multiple streams is a promising approach for on-line handwritten text recognition.
the discrete HMMs are more sensitive to the choice of the feature quantization.
multiple stream HMM systems are more robust to feature quantization errors than single stream HMMs, which is an important result in the context of on-line handwriting recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice of the features is as important as the choice of the quantization and the HMM structure.
multiple stream HMM systems are a good choice for on-line handwritten recognition of whiteboard notes.
the choice of the features to be quantized in a multiple stream HMM system is as important as the proper quantization of the features themselves.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proper choice of features for the individual streams is crucial for the performance of multiple stream HMM systems.

the choice of the features to be used in an on-line handwriting recognition system is not as straightforward as it seems at first sight: the statistical properties of the features have to be taken into account in order to obtain the best performance.

the use of a discrete multiple stream HMM is an interesting alternative to continuous HMMs, especially in cases where the number of states is very large and the number of training examples is limited.
